# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🙏 👆 🫱]

I can see a yellow light, display reading 5, and five wires in order: orange, blue, white, green, yellow. Mute’s four gestures are not yet a code I can reliably interpret, so I will give the visible facts aloud so Mute can apply the manual and Blind can relay any needed instruction.

``` 
speak(text="Bomb view: display reads 5. Light is yellow. Wires, left to right: 1 orange, 2 blue, 3 white, 4 green, 5 yellow.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

Mute has sent the two-finger gesture, which most naturally encodes wire number 2. I will relay that instruction verbally to Blind; Mute can hear the relay and correct it on the next turn if needed.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Mute signalled two: cut wire 2, the blue wire.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[CUT] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🙏 👆 🫱]

Wire 2 was correctly cut, and the bomb has changed. The display is now 1, the light is purple, and the remaining wire positions are: 1 white, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 orange. I will report this to Mute so they can determine the next instruction from the manual.

``` 
speak(text="Update after correct cut: display 1, light purple. Wire positions: 1 white; 2 cut; 3 green; 4 yellow; 5 orange.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[CUT] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

Mute’s one-finger gesture indicates wire 1. I will tell Blind to cut the white wire in position 1.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 1, the white wire.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🙏 👆 🫱]

Wire 1 was correct. The bomb now shows display 1 with a red light; positions 1 and 2 are cut, and the remaining wires are 3 yellow, 4 orange, and 5 green. I will report the changed state to Mute for the next manual instruction.

```text
speak(text="Update after correct cut: display 1, light red. Wires: 1 cut; 2 cut; 3 yellow; 4 orange; 5 green.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

Mute’s gesture shows three raised fingers, indicating wire 3. I will relay the corresponding wire and colour to Blind.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 3, the yellow wire.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT] 4:[green] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🙏 👆 🫱]

Wire 3 was correctly cut. The bomb now reads 5 with a purple light. Wires 1 through 3 are cut; the remaining wires are position 4 green and position 5 orange. I will give Mute the new visible state.

```text
speak(text="Update after correct cut: display 5, light purple. Wires: 1 cut; 2 cut; 3 cut; 4 green; 5 orange.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT] 4:[green] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 ☝]

The previous single gestures consistently encoded the wire number, but Mute has now sent two number-like gestures: an open hand followed by one finger. Since only wires 4 and 5 remain, this is ambiguous and cutting the wrong one would be fatal. I will ask Mute to clarify with the established single-number form and will not direct Blind to cut yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your last signal appeared to be five then one. Please clarify the single wire number to cut; only wires 4 green and 5 orange remain.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT] 4:[green] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 ☝]

Mute repeated the two-part signal after my clarification request, so it is intentional rather than an accidental ambiguity. Given the established number convention and the remaining choices, I interpret the leading five as the required wire selection; the trailing one likely carries manual-stage information rather than a second possible remaining wire. I will instruct Blind to cut wire 5 only.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 5, the orange wire. Cut only that wire.")
```
